name: Platform Foundation Architecture Practice
description: This practice governs the foundational construction of the Internal Developer Platform. It focuses on the rigorous selection of upstream CNCF components, the configuration of advanced multi-cluster networking capabilities, and the critical restructuring of traditional infrastructure teams into a unified, product-centric platform organization.

narratives.name: Foundational IDP Architecture
narratives.description: The overarching context for transitioning foundational infrastructure to standard CNCF abstractions.

narrativeContexts.context: Historically, infrastructure and operations organizations operated in technology-aligned silos, maintaining distinct teams for compute, networking, and continuous delivery. This outdated structure generates massive friction, requiring application developers to file multiple asynchronous tickets across different departments simply to deploy a standard microservice.

To successfully build, maintain, and scale an effective IDP, the organization must adopt a cross-functional model based on the principles of Team Topologies, focusing entirely on the end-to-end developer experience and effectively operating as an internal product company serving captive enterprise customers.

Technologically, this transition demands the replacement of legacy ingress controllers and proprietary routing logic with the highly portable, expressive, and extensible Kubernetes Gateway API. This role-oriented design cleanly separates the responsibilities of infrastructure providers, cluster operators, and application developers.

Ultimately, the platform must adhere strictly to standard orchestration interfaces and Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs), ensuring deep ecosystem interoperability, the prevention of tool sprawl, and true operational portability across disparate cloud environments.

narratives.name: The Dissolution of Silos
narratives.description: The rationale for moving away from technology-aligned operational teams.

narrativeContexts.context: A technically flawless Kubernetes architecture will inevitably fail to deliver value if the organizational structure responsible for maintaining it is misaligned.

Historically, operations organizations maintained distinct teams for compute, networking, and CI/CD. This outdated structure generates massive friction, requiring developers to navigate convoluted approval processes across different departments.
The primary reason internal platforms fail is not due to technological inadequacy, but rather organizing the platform around technology stacks instead of user needs.

To effectively scale the IDP, the organization must adopt a cross-functional model, effectively operating as an internal product company serving captive enterprise customers through cohesive, interdisciplinary units.

alphas.name: Platform
alphas.description: The unified system of upstream CNCF assets, declarative multicluster management engines, and network interfaces provided to internal consumers as a cohesive service.

narratives.name: Component Selection Strategy
narratives.description: The framework and criteria utilized for selecting foundational platform components.

narrativeContexts.context: The selection process for building an internal developer platform from the CNCF ecosystem is a highly complex architectural exercise requiring rigorous evaluation criteria to prevent tooling sprawl and fragmented operational states.

Components must be evaluated primarily on composability and loose coupling, allowing product teams to consume only the specific capabilities they explicitly need while gracefully falling back to standard Kubernetes primitives if abstractions prove inadequate.

Tools must rely on standard Kubernetes Custom Resource Definitions rather than proprietary sidecars, closed-source agents, or non-standard APIs that introduce deep vendor lock-in and compromise operational portability.

Furthermore, chosen projects must possess deep, API-level integration symmetry to ensure the platform operates as a cohesive unit. For instance, ensuring that GitOps controllers natively understand the Custom Resources generated by the multicluster management engines.

checklist.name: CNCF Maturity Verified
checklist.description: All selected primary platform components reside in the Graduated or Incubating tiers of the CNCF landscape, guaranteeing transparent governance and rigorous security auditing.

checklist.name: Standard Interfaces Confirmed
checklist.description: The architecture strictly utilizes standard Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) without reliance on proprietary agents or closed-source extensions.

checklist.name: Gateway API Adopted
checklist.description: The architectural blueprint standardizes on the Kubernetes Gateway API rather than legacy Ingress to handle Layer 7 load balancing, TLS termination, and advanced traffic splitting.

checklist.name: Composability Assessed
checklist.description: The chosen abstraction layers allow application teams to gracefully fall back to native Kubernetes primitives if the abstraction does not suit their unique edge-case architectures.

checklist.name: Declarative Multicluster Management
checklist.description: Cluster API (CAPI) manifests are defined to manage the underlying compute fabric, including control plane nodes and Kubernetes versions, declaratively.

checklist.name: Role-Oriented Networking Configured
checklist.description: The GatewayClass resources are explicitly defined by infrastructure providers to establish the underlying physical load balancer implementations.

checklist.name: External Resource Reconciliation Defined
checklist.description: Active, infinite reconciliation loops utilizing operators like Crossplane are configured to monitor external cloud resources and prevent configuration drift.

checklist.name: Pull-Based GitOps Operational
checklist.description: The GitOps controller (Argo CD or Flux) is securely installed inside the cluster boundary and actively pulling synchronized state from the designated single source of truth repository.

checklist.name: Infrastructure Tests Executing
checklist.description: Kubernetes-native testing frameworks are executing validation jobs within the live network topology to confirm scheduling constraints and service discovery mechanisms.

checklist.name: Active Reconciliation Loops Validated
checklist.description: Operators are successfully detecting manual configuration drift via cloud consoles and autonomously reverting external resources back to the desired declared state.

checklist.name: Cluster Upgrades Automated
checklist.description: The platform team can execute Kubernetes version upgrades across multiple clusters simultaneously by updating centralized Git repositories.

checklist.name: Gateway Endpoints Established
checklist.description: Cluster operators have successfully deployed Gateway objects defining specific network endpoints, listeners, and TLS configurations.

checklist.name: Load Validation Completed
checklist.description: Distributed load-testing jobs (utilizing tools like the k6-operator) have confirmed that infrastructure configurations meet stringent latency and throughput requirements prior to promotion.

states.name: Hosting Assets
states.description: The platform is actively supporting workloads.

alphas.name: Platform Consumption Interface
alphas.description: The unified developer portals, internal APIs, and visualization dashboards that abstract the complexity of raw Kubernetes from the end-user.

checklist.name: Developer Friction Mapped
checklist.description: Deep user experience research has quantitatively tracked where developers experience the most friction and cognitive load in legacy delivery systems.

checklist.name: Visualization Requirements Defined
checklist.description: Requirements for real-time operational troubleshooting, distinctly separating administrator needs from developer needs, are documented.

checklist.name: Portal Framework Selected
checklist.description: A centralized software catalog and scaffolding engine, such as Backstage, is selected for core integration.

checklist.name: RBAC Mapping Outlined
checklist.description: Interface visualization tools are scoped to strictly honor the user's existing Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) permissions across multiple namespaces and clusters.

checklist.name: Lightweight UI Deployed
checklist.description: Tools like Headlamp or OpenLens are successfully deployed, providing granular multi-tenant views without the heavy memory consumption associated with desktop-heavy applications.

checklist.name: Centralized Catalog Active
checklist.description: The Internal Developer Portal is running, properly authenticated, and successfully querying the underlying Kubernetes APIs for active resources.

states.name: Self Service
states.description: Consumers can independently use the interface.

states.name: Optimized
states.description: The interface provides a frictionless experience.

alphas.name: Team
alphas.description: The cross-functional organization structured to build, maintain, and scale the Internal Developer Platform as an internal product company.

checklist.name: Executive Sponsorship Acquired
checklist.description: Executive leaders actively champion the platform's usage and mandate the shift away from erratic, voluntary tool usage.

checklist.name: Silo Dissolution Acknowledged
checklist.description: The organization acknowledges that legacy infrastructure silos (compute, networking, CI/CD) must be restructured to reduce deployment friction.

checklist.name: Product Manager Assigned
checklist.description: A Platform Product Manager is appointed to prioritize the engineering roadmap based on quantitative usage metrics and qualitative feedback.

checklist.name: DevEx Engineers Identified
checklist.description: Software engineers are dedicated to writing glue code, internal APIs, and maintaining the developer portal interfaces.

checklist.name: Embedded Developers Included
checklist.description: Highly skilled application developers from enterprise workload teams are brought into the platform team on a rotational basis to provide immediate UX feedback.

checklist.name: Feedback Loops Established
checklist.description: Direct user engagement methods, such as structured developer surveys and targeted ride-along observation sessions, are actively operating.

checklist.name: Interdisciplinary Workflows Active
checklist.description: Infrastructure engineers and DevEx engineers collaboratively abstract complex multi-cluster APIs into intuitive self-service portals.

states.name: Adjourned
states.description: The team is disbanded or repurposed.

workProducts.name: Platform Architecture Blueprint
workProducts.description: The comprehensive logical and executable design detailing the integration of CNCF components, networking topologies, and infrastructure-as-code manifests.

levelsOfDetail.name: Outlined
levelsOfDetail.description: Basic identification of CNCF ecosystem alternatives mapped against proprietary PaaS capabilities.

checklist.name: Component Mapping Documented
checklist.description: Core functionalities (Routing, Policy, Builds) are explicitly mapped to upstream alternatives (Gateway API, Kyverno, Shipwright) based on ecosystem evaluation.

checklist.name: Integration Tax Assessed
checklist.description: The effort required by the internal team to ensure distinct open-source software components interoperate is formally estimated.

levelsOfDetail.name: Detailed
levelsOfDetail.description: Logical architectures displaying the exact API interactions between GitOps controllers, networking boundaries, and multi-cluster management loops.

checklist.name: Role-Oriented Networking Modeled
checklist.description: The strict separation of GatewayClass, Gateway, and HTTPRoute management across infrastructure, operations, and developer personas is diagrammed.

checklist.name: Reconciliation Loops Defined
checklist.description: The architecture logically specifies how active, infinite reconciliation loops will continuously monitor and revert external configuration drift.

levelsOfDetail.name: Executable
levelsOfDetail.description: Fully deployable, validated Infrastructure-as-Code and GitOps manifests that instantiate the architecture.

checklist.name: Declarative Manifests Created
checklist.description: The entire multicluster compute fabric is defined in version-controlled YAML manifests utilizing Cluster API definitions.

checklist.name: Pull-Based Integration Validated
checklist.description: The architecture is executable via intelligent agents residing securely inside the cluster pulling from the single source of truth.

workProducts.name: Team Topology Charter
workProducts.description: The strategic blueprint defining the structure, interaction modes, and service boundaries of the internal platform organization.

levelsOfDetail.name: Outlined
levelsOfDetail.description: Basic identification of the necessary roles and the high-level rationale for organizational change.

checklist.name: Friction Points Documented
checklist.description: Legacy asynchronous ticketing workflows across departments are documented as organizational anti-patterns.

checklist.name: Core Roles Identified
checklist.description: Required specializations (Product Manager, DevEx, SRE Leads) are identified to replace traditional sysadmin roles.

levelsOfDetail.name: Defined
levelsOfDetail.description: Detailed role templates, responsibilities, and specific interaction models based on product-centric principles.

checklist.name: Service Boundaries Defined
checklist.description: The specific autonomous services the platform team provides to the stream-aligned application teams are clearly codified.

checklist.name: Rotational Programs Formalized
checklist.description: The cadence, duration, and structure for embedding application developers into the platform team is documented.

activities.name: Evaluate CNCF Interoperability
activities.description: Systematically assess upstream CNCF projects against criteria of composability, maturity, and integration symmetry to formulate the platform architecture.

narratives.name: Preventing Tool Sprawl
narratives.description: How architects evaluate projects to avoid operational fragmentation.

narrativeContexts.context: Unlike purchasing a vendor-curated distribution where integration testing is guaranteed by the provider, internal architects must establish rigorous evaluation criteria to prevent disjointed tooling.

The team conducts deep evaluations prioritizing CNCF Graduated and Incubating projects, explicitly verifying that tools possess deep API-level integrations with one another to prevent operational friction at scale.

activities.name: Provision Declarative Multicluster Infrastructure
activities.description: Implement GitOps controllers, Cluster APIs, and role-oriented Gateway network configurations to establish the immutable platform fabric.

activities.name: Deploy Developer Portal and Visualization
activities.description: Install and configure software catalogs (Backstage) and cluster visualization UIs (Headlamp) strictly mapped to existing multi-tenant RBAC.

activities.name: Design Platform Team Topology
activities.description: Restructure technology-aligned silos into a cross-functional, product-focused platform organization featuring embedded developer rotations.

personas.name: Platform Product Manager
personas.description: Treats the IDP as a discrete software product and internal developers as valued customers. Responsible for ruthlessly prioritizing the engineering roadmap based on quantitative metrics and qualitative research.

personas.name: Infrastructure Engineer
personas.description: Deep domain experts in container orchestration, Gateway APIs, and IaC. They do not manually deploy applications, but construct the declarative systems that allow workloads to deploy themselves autonomously.

personas.name: DevEx Engineer
personas.description: Software engineers focused on the developer experience. They write the necessary glue code, build internal APIs, and maintain the Backstage portal to ensure complex infrastructure interfaces are cleanly abstracted.

personaGroups.name: Platform Leadership
personaGroups.description: Executives and Product Managers guiding the socio-technical transformation.

personaGroups.name: Platform Core Engineering
personaGroups.description: The deeply specialized team handling multicluster management, network controllers, and compute state.

personaGroups.name: Developer Experience Engineering
personaGroups.description: The bridging team focused entirely on abstracting APIs into intuitive, self-service portals.

personaGroups.name: Platform Architecture Board
personaGroups.description: Senior technical staff responsible for evaluating upstream CNCF components for interoperability.

patterns.name: IDP Foundation Establishment Lifecycle
patterns.description: The sequential phases required to strategically move from proprietary PaaS distributions to a stable, highly available upstream CNCF platform fabric.

narratives.name: The Infrastructure Migration
narratives.description: The overarching journey of decoupling developer experience from underlying infrastructure.

narrativeContexts.context: The transition begins with a rigorous evaluation phase, acknowledging the organizational friction caused by legacy infrastructure silos and mapping specific commercial features to CNCF equivalents.
Subsequently, the organization forms a product-centric platform team tasked with declaring the new multicluster compute fabric entirely in version-controlled manifests.
Finally, developer portals and visualization tools are activated, bridging the gap between raw, powerful infrastructure and necessary developer simplicity.

patternViews.name: Prerequisites
patternViews.description: Securing executive mandate and identifying existing organizational friction prior to technical selection.

patternViews.name: Architecture & Design Phase
patternViews.description: Rigorous selection of CNCF tools and the explicit definition of the new operational team topologies.

patternViews.name: Infrastructure Provisioning Phase
patternViews.description: Declarative configuration, continuous validation, and automated deployment of the base multicluster fabric.

patternViews.name: Interface Activation Phase
patternViews.description: Secure deployment of developer portals and integration of cross-functional team workflows.
